card.summary: The Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026 requires the Environmental Protection Agency to reinstate specific environmental and public health regulations, programs, and guidance that were in effect on January 19, 2025. The bill sets restrictions against future deregulatory delays, mandates the use of peer-reviewed science and specific values for the social cost of carbon, restores scientific advisory boards, sets enforcement funding floors, expands environmental justice programs, and allows private citizens to bring civil actions in federal court if the agency fails to comply.
card.title: Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026

latest_action.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

summary: The Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026 directs the Environmental Protection Agency to reinstate specific environmental and public health regulations, guidance, and enforcement programs that were in effect on January 19, 2025. It prohibits federal officials from weakening or delaying these standards without explicit congressional authorization. Furthermore, the bill mandates the restoration of scientific advisory boards, use of the social cost of carbon, specific enforcement funding levels, and environmental justice programs.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with reinstated federal emissions limits, reporting requirements, and air toxics standards that were in place as of January 19, 2025, and face restrictions on federal rollbacks of these rules.
affected_groups.group: Regulated industries (power plants, oil and gas operations, and vehicle manufacturers)

affected_groups.effect: Receive prioritized monitoring, permitting oversight, and enforcement from the EPA under environmental justice provisions.
Must be reconstituted and fully staffed with members free of financial or advisory ties to regulated industries.
affected_groups.group: Scientific advisory bodies (Science Advisory Board and Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee)

key_provisions: Requires the EPA Administrator to fully reinstate all regulations, guidance, and enforcement programs related to greenhouse gases, methane, mercury and air toxics, national ambient air quality standards, greenhouse gas reporting, and vehicle emissions that were in effect on January 19, 2025, within 60 days of enactment.
Bans the President, the EPA Administrator, and other federal officials from delaying, suspending, repealing, or weakening these reinstated regulations without explicit congressional authorization.

Requires the EPA Administrator to reconstitute and fully staff the Science Advisory Board and the Clean Air Scientific Advisory Committee with members not financially or advisory-associated with regulated industries, and mandates the use of peer-reviewed science and a specific social cost of carbon ($190 per metric ton with a 2 percent discount rate).
Authorizes $10,993,653,000 (adjusted annually for inflation) for fiscal year 2027 and each year thereafter to ensure sufficient civil and criminal enforcement personnel and funding at the EPA.

Mandates the restoration and expansion of eliminated or defunded environmental justice programs, prioritizing monitoring and enforcement in communities with disproportionate pollution burdens and requiring public health impact assessments for rulemakings.

Creates a private right of action allowing any adversely affected person to bring a civil action in a U.S. district court to compel compliance with the Act, with potential awards for reasonable attorney's fees.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Environmental Health Restoration Act of 2026 directs the Environmental Protection Agency to reinstate specific environmental and public health regulations, guidance, and enforcement programs that were in effect on January 19, 2025. It prohibits federal officials from weakening or delaying these standards without explicit congressional authorization. Furthermore, the bill mandates the restoration of scientific advisory boards, use of the social cost of carbon, specific enforcement funding levels, and environmental justice programs.
summary_detail.significance: The bill mandates a large-scale legal and operational reversal of federal environmental deregulation by legally locking in specific 2025 standards, setting a multi-billion dollar funding floor for EPA enforcement, and creating broad judicial review options for private citizens to compel agency compliance.
